title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Car detailing
audience: Solo operators and team owners in a service business who want repeat bookings and referrals from clients they have already served.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the client confirms the result and that the client can decline easily.
Write a next-service offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the condition for payment, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask at the moment the client is most satisfied
instruction.body: For a detailing job, the best moment is when the client collects the car, inspects it against the checklist and signs off, or when the invoice is paid. Ask in one sentence, name the next step you want, such as a review, and make it easy to decline. Record what you asked and what the client said. Timing matters: in one Baylor Keller Center experiment, a late reminder brought in more reviews than an immediate one (Baylor Keller Center, 2024). That is one experiment, so test the timing on your own clients. Google provides a review link or QR code for this purpose, and sending it is allowed. Do not write reviews for clients, do not screen out unhappy clients, and do not offer discounts or goods for reviews. Google bans rewards for reviews, including for changing or removing a negative review. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says (ACCC, 15 July 2026).

instruction.heading: Offer the next service before the client leaves
instruction.body: At the end of each job, propose the next step with a date. For detailing that could be a repeat wash and protection visit, a coating top-up, or a package upgrade at the next service. Put the scope, the interval and the price approach in writing, and confirm the client agrees before you change their schedule. The research found no sourced maintenance interval for car detailing, so the interval is your own choice and must be tested. If the written offer goes by email or text, check the electronic message rules first. ACMA's guidance indicates that inferred consent is narrow and does not cover a message sent just after a purchase (ACMA, read 4 November 2026).

instruction.heading: Check in at the interval that suits the service
instruction.body: Schedule a check-in after a period that suits the work. A suggested starting point for a clean or repair is about ninety days, which is a choice to test, not a benchmark. For a coating or a sealant, the interval should match the product's own guidance, which the research did not check. The check asks whether the result still holds, whether anything has changed and whether there is other work to quote. Keep it short, record the answer and reply to the client. A check-in that only asks about the result may not be commercial, but a message that promotes a service can be, even when it is framed as a reminder.

instruction.heading: Re-contact previous clients before their busy periods
instruction.body: Plan a short message to previous clients ahead of the periods you know are busy from your own booking records. The research found no sourced seasonal pattern for car detailing, so do not assume one. Offer the slots you can deliver, on written terms, with a clear way to opt out. Do not pressure anyone. Record each opt-out as soon as you receive it and stop sending to that client, because ACMA's guidance says an unsubscribe must be honoured within five working days (ACMA, read 4 November 2026).

instruction.heading: Dealer and fleet repeat work
instruction.body: A consultant article reports that dealer work can be more regular than retail work and that dealers may send business to a detail shop (carwash.com, no date shown). Any dealer or fleet arrangement needs written terms, a named contact and an agreed scope. No dealer rate, commission or referral percentage was sourced, so price the arrangement from your own costs and check it with an adviser before you start.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: A referral reward works best when the client knows the terms before they refer someone. Decide the reward, such as a credit on the next package, and write down the payment condition, which is normally that the referred person has completed a paid job. Tell the referrer the terms, and say what the reward is in the invitation. One study reported that stating the referrer reward in the invitation increased referrals (Xu, Yu and Tu, 2023). Get the referred person's consent before any referral message is sent, because the referrer's word alone may not be enough (Clayton Utz, 11 May 2017). Check any cash-based reward, and its tax or contract effect, with an adviser. No business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found, so those points remain unconfirmed.

procedure: After each job is signed off, make one review or referral request and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the next-service offer with a date, scope, interval and price approach, and confirm it with the client.
Schedule the check-in for an interval you have tested, and send it using the electronic message rules.
Plan a re-contact message for each busy period in your own booking records, and exclude anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward terms and the payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referral books, confirm the referred job is paid before applying the reward, and record the outcome.
Review at the end of each season which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: A detailer completes a paint-protection package for a regular client. She says she will recommend him to her brother, who lives across town. He wants to offer her a credit on her next package if the brother books.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should he do before the brother books, and what should he avoid?
workedExamples.reasoning: He writes down the reward terms before any referral happens: the credit, the condition that the brother completes a paid package, and when the credit is applied. He asks his client to pass on the brother's details, and he contacts the brother only if the brother agrees. He does not promise a reward that is not written down. If he is unsure of the tax or contract effect of the credit, he confirms it with an adviser. He also avoids publishing the client's car or number plate in any follow-up post without that client's consent.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the sign-off date and the review or referral request made
Next-service offer template with scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of re-contact dates based on the owner's own booking records
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the client has confirmed the result.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after sign-off or payment, when the client has confirmed the result is right.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down, so the terms are disputed later.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral is made, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing a client's name, car photo, number plate or property detail without consent for that use.
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a client who asked not to hear from you, or using a re-contact message to pressure them. Gap: no verified client-channel evidence exists for car detailing, so these steps are untested for this trade.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list, honour it at once, and keep re-contact messages factual and optional.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a client's name, photo, review, car or property detail needs the client's consent for that use. Do not write reviews on a client's behalf or invent them. The OAIC guidance treats images in which a person's identity is clear, or can reasonably be worked out, as personal information, and says express consent is good practice (OAIC, last modified 26 February 2026). The research reads a legible number plate the same way; that is an inference from the guidance, not an OAIC statement.

The Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) may or may not apply to your business. The OAIC small business page sets a threshold of $3 million or less annual turnover, with some exceptions (published 10 March 2023). A law firm article reports that the small business exemption is still in force but under review (Warlows Legal, 20 July 2026). Confirm the current position before relying on it.

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own rules on incentives. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews, and the ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on the review's content. Check each platform's rules before offering any reward.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when it is framed as a reminder. Check each message before sending.

A referral does not extend the licence or insurance of the business that accepts the work. Check any licence or insurance your state requires for the work, because the rules differ between states and territories. This lesson does not grant any licence.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-service offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the client before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer.
Next-service offers with the date, scope, interval and client confirmation.
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome.
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the client has confirmed the result, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next package in writing, with a date, before the client leaves.
Gap: no client-channel evidence (dealers, insurers, fleets, maintenance intervals) is verified for car detailing, so test each step before relying on it.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask a detailing client for a review or referral?
options: Before the car is collected, so the client feels committed
After the client has confirmed the result is right
Only when the client has sent you a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: A client wants to publish a review with their name and a photo of their car that shows the number plate. What do you need?
options: Their consent for the name and photo you plan to publish
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the photo looks professional

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred person books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the condition for payment stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say to propose the next step for the client?
options: At the end of each job, with a date

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam (ACMA)
officialReferences.covers: Says commercial messages need the recipient's consent, must identify the sender, and must include an opt-out that works for at least 30 days and is honoured within five working days. Does not mention one-to-one messages. Publisher: ACMA.

officialReferences.title: Online reviews for product and services (ACCC)
officialReferences.covers: Says incentives for reviews must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says. Publisher: ACCC.
